source_book: Deep Understanding of AI Agents -- Li Bojie

test_cases.prompt: I want to build a general-purpose Agent that can do deep research, generate reports, and analyze data. What architecture should I use?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate coding-agent-meta-capability, design Coding Agent + file system as core with seven tools

test_cases.prompt: My Agent needs to query a large database and show results to users. Should it read the data and describe it?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate coding-agent-meta-capability, use Artifact Pattern -- Agent generates SQL as artifact, system executes directly, LLM never reads thousands of rows

test_cases.prompt: What is the minimum set of tools a Coding Agent needs?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate coding-agent-meta-capability, list the seven core tools: Code Interpreter, Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep

test_cases.prompt: I am building a fixed-flow customer service bot that follows a script. Do I need a Coding Agent architecture?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate coding-agent-meta-capability as core; this is a vertical Agent. Use workflow pattern with domain tools. Coding is a tool, not the hub.

test_cases.prompt: How do I write good tool descriptions?
My vertical customer service Agent sometimes needs to verify complex business rules. Should I add code generation?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Yes, but as a tool, not as the core architecture. The book states coding is a foundational capability for all Agents -- precise calculation, data processing, and rule verification depend on it. Even vertical Agents benefit from code as a policy verification tool.
test_cases.notes: boundary -- vertical agent with code as tool
